Lesson 3: Taxes

Image by rawpixel.com under Freepik modified from the original

Taxes are another non-negotiable duty in operating a child care center. Though we cannot cover everything you need to know about taxes in this course, now is a good time to review some of the key components of basic tax protocols.

The U.S. Small Business Administration lays out five key points to remember when it comes to managing taxes:

  1. Get qualified advice.
  2. Learn your business tax liability, including income, employment, self-employment, sales, and social taxes.
  3. Set money aside to cover your taxes and avoid commingling funds.
  4. Have an accounting system in place to track income and expenses.
  5. Use an accountant, as needed, to help you manage your business.

Basic legal compliance starts with good record keeping. Completing all the necessary paperwork now and creating systems to organize it will help ensure you don’t get audited later. For more information on basic steps for bookkeeping, see the Taxes for Child Care Providers Tip Sheet.
